classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied right triangle to relate string length and horizontal displacement, recover x=60 and connect the rates.

content.prompt:
A boy flies a kite $80\text{ m}$ above the ground and the wind blows it on a horizontal course at $5\text{ m/s}$.

Find how fast the string is being let out when the kite is $100\text{ m}$ from him.

spec.description: Dashed vertical height and horizontal displacement meet at a right angle; the solid string rises to the right. The wind arrow points horizontally right. Source ochre string is ordinary geometry and is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: A right triangle has vertical side 80 m, horizontal side x and hypotenuse s; dx/dt=5 m/s.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is supplied in the question.

answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the string length and $x$ the horizontal displacement. Then $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=5\text{ m/s}$ and
$$\begin{aligned}s^2&=x^2+80^2\\s&=\sqrt{x^2+80^2}\\\frac{ds}{dx}&=\frac{2x}{2\sqrt{x^2+80^2}}\\&=\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+80^2}}\\\frac{ds}{dt}&=\frac{ds}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=\frac{5x}{\sqrt{x^2+80^2}}.\end{aligned}$$
When $s=100$,
$$\begin{aligned}x^2+6400&=10000\\x&=60.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{ds}{dt}&=\frac{5(60)}{\sqrt{60^2+80^2}}\\&=3\text{ m/s}.\end{aligned}$$
